title: Replace Constructor with Factory Function

solutions.title: A private constructor behind three named factories
solutions.tradeoff: One general-purpose constructor call becomes three named factory methods plus a small dispatcher for the one caller that only has a runtime string to go on, so a fourth ticket kind now means touching four places instead of one, and a reader has to learn which of the four to use instead of always writing `new Ticket(...)`.

reviewFocus: Is `Ticket`'s constructor actually `private`, so `tsc` rejects a stray `new Ticket(...)` from outside `ticket.ts` - or is it only conventionally off-limits?
Does exactly one switch on `TicketType` survive, inside the batch dispatcher, or did a second one creep back into a caller that could have used a named factory instead?
Does `issueCompTicket` fail by returning `null`, or did the refactor leave a path where the old constructor's `throw` is still reachable from a caller that expects it can't happen?
Does the walkthrough admit the real cost - more names to keep straight, and a fourth ticket kind touching four places - rather than presenting the factories as a free win?
Does the walkthrough read `drill-10-04` and say plainly when this drill's dispatcher should graduate into that one's polymorphism, instead of implying the two moves are the same thing?
